extracted.intended_audience: authors and editors of Cochrane (and other) systematic reviews of healthcare interventions; review teams preparing or maintaining Cochrane intervention reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and core methodological expectations for planning, conducting, analysing, and interpreting Cochrane systematic reviews of interventions, including specialized topics (non-randomized studies, adverse effects, equity, etc.). Intended to be the authoritative methodological handbook for review authors and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning a review
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the standard methods applicable to planning a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes guidance on the standard methods applicable to every review (planning a review, searching and selecting studies, data collection, risk of bias assessment, statistical analysis, GRADE and interpreting results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching and selecting studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and methods for designing and conducting systematic searches and selecting studies for inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Handbook's standard methods for every review; covers how to search for and select relevant studies to include in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and standards for collecting data from included studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on data collection approaches that are standard for Cochrane reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the risk of bias in included studies using appropriate tools and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook provides guidance on risk of bias assessment as a core methodological component of every review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for statistical synthesis and meta-analysis of study results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers statistical analysis techniques appropriate for combining study results and exploring heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE and interpreting results
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) for rating certainty of evidence and guidance on interpreting review results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes guidance on GRADE and interpreting results as part of standard review methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-randomized studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialised guidance for including and assessing non-randomized studies of interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook addresses more specialised topics including non-randomized studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on identifying, extracting, analysing, and reporting adverse effects of interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adverse effects are listed among the specialised topics covered by the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for handling complexity in interventions (e.g., multi-component interventions, interactions, contextual factors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes guidance for complex interventions as a specialised topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of equity issues in reviews, including how interventions may affect different populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity is included as one of the specialised topics the Handbook covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for incorporating economic evidence (costs, cost-effectiveness) into systematic reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economics is listed among the specialised topics in the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient-reported outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on handling, analysing, and interpreting patient-reported outcome measures within reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patient-reported outcomes are included as a specialised topic covered by the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and considerations for conducting meta-analyses using individual participant data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual patient data is explicitly listed among the specialised topics in the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on planning and conducting prospective meta-analyses where studies are identified and included before results are known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective meta-analysis is included among the specialised topics covered by the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative research
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches for integrating and appraising qualitative research within or alongside intervention reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative research methods and considerations are listed as a specialised topic in the Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological Expectations for Cochrane Intervention Reviews (MECIR) — core standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Key aspects of Handbook guidance collated as MECIR, which provide core standards generally expected of Cochrane reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each MECIR item includes a link to a relevant Handbook chapter; MECIR items summarise core standards that are generally expected of Cochrane reviews.
